title: Start here: source hierarchy and reading workflow
summary: Use primary protocol and IBM sources before implementation folklore. RFC 1205 defines the base 5250 Telnet interface and explicitly delegates the workstation data stream to IBM SA21-9247. RFC 4777 supplies current published TN5250E/iSeries Telnet enhancements and obsoletes RFC 2877. IBM i documentation is operational authority for current IBM i server/client behaviour. Historical SA21-9247 editions remain the principal data-stream reference, with RFC 1205 section 5 carrying corrections/enhancements to SA21-9247-6.
procedure: For Telnet framing/negotiation, start with RFC 1205.
For TN5250E device naming, environment negotiation, auto-signon, password substitution/encryption and printer extensions, start with RFC 4777; use RFC 2877 only for history/delta archaeology.
For 5250 commands/orders/fields/AID/error/help semantics, navigate SA21-9247-6 and then check RFC 1205 section 5 for corrections/enhancements.
For current IBM i operational behaviour, verify against IBM Documentation for the applicable IBM i release.
Keep printed/manual page numbers distinct from physical PDF pages; use Gopher reference locate/read/move rather than guessing offsets.
invariants: A link is a locator, not evidence that a claimed behaviour exists; open and read the bounded source.
RFC 2877 is obsolete and must not silently override RFC 4777.
RFC 1205 and RFC 4777 do not replace the IBM 5250 data-stream manual.
Historical manual wording and current IBM i behaviour are separate authority layers.
authority: project-reference-doctrine grounded in RFC Editor, IBM publication metadata, and IBM Documentation
